gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much power each inverter uses just to stay on. At a pellet stove's 150 W, that idle draw changes the order of the 'longest runtime' list. The BLUETTI Apex 300 + B300K (5,529.6 Wh, about 19.5 W idle) runs about 29 h, which matches or beats the larger EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra (6,144 Wh, 45–60 W idle) at about 26–28 h. The Anker SOLIX F3800 (70–80 W idle) falls from ChatGPT's 21.8 h to about 15 h.
standout_why: I compared against the cited solarwaypoint.com three-way table, which lists rated Wh, total cycles and UPS transfer time (20/0/30 ms) but has no idle or self-consumption row. Its cycle counts (3,000/6,000/3,500) also don't say what capacity is left at the end of those cycles, so they can't be compared directly. I also checked ChatGPT's own answers in both chats: they divide rated Wh by 150 W at a flat 85% and ignore idle draw. Our current page has measured usable Wh at 200–1,000 W, but no idle column, and it doesn't cover the DELTA Pro Ultra or F3800. EcoFlow's US store and Anker's F3800 Plus page state no self-consumption figure. BLUETTI is the only maker that publishes one (≈20 W) and a runtime formula that adds it to the load. I could not read the two cited enoughwatts.com pages (SSL certificate error), so I can't rule out that they mention idle draw.
decides: For 'runs a pellet stove the longest', the overall top pick stays the same: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X (12,288 Wh, about 36 W idle) at roughly 56 h at 150 W (12,288 × 0.90 ÷ 186). Below that, ranking by rated Wh is wrong at stove-level loads. The Apex 300 + B300K ($2,599 at BLUETTI, 2026-11-15) ties or beats a DELTA Pro Ultra ($3,799 list, shown unavailable) on hours, for $1,200 less. The F3800 drops to about the same runtime as a single Apex 300. The page should rank by hours = Wh × 0.90 ÷ (stove W + idle W), not by Wh.

findings.label: Hours at a 150 W stove, counting idle draw
findings.source_title: BLUETTI formula applied to the idle figures above
findings.note: Rated Wh × 0.90 ÷ (150 + idle W), with DoD left out. Examples: 12,288 × 0.9 ÷ 186; 8,294.4 × 0.9 ÷ 169.5; 5,529.6 × 0.9 ÷ 169.5; 6,144 × 0.9 ÷ 195 or ÷ 210; 3,840 × 0.9 ÷ 230 or ÷ 220; 2,764.8 × 0.9 ÷ 169.5. These are estimates. The η = 0.90 at load and the no-load idle figure may partly double-count losses, so treat the gap between units as more reliable than the exact hours. ChatGPT gave 34.8 h (DPU), 21.8 h (F3800) and 15.7 h (Apex 300) without counting idle draw.
